_readme: Single source of truth for everything that is specific to THIS constituency.
Read by the Worker (src/hyd_config.ts) and by the Python importers
(hyd_import/*.py), so the part mapping cannot drift between them.
To point this deployment at a different constituency, change this file —
not the TypeScript or Python. Anything still hardcoded is a bug; say so.
- SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS lives in wrangler.jsonc. It is a deploy-time env var
on purpose, so a mistake in a data file can never lock out every admin.
- Cloudflare resource names and ids also live in wrangler.jsonc.
- src/comprehensive_search.ts and public/js/search-all.js carry their own
old/new part maps. Those serve the FIRST-generation tabs, which read the
electors/asddo/draft_sir tables and are empty and hidden in this
deployment. They are dormant here and deliberately not wired to this
file; if you ever un-hide that area, wire them up or delete them.

_part_offset: Secunderabad is +1: the 2026 draft inserted a new part 148 at the front,
shifting every later part up by one. Verified from the polling-station
section lists, and independently by EPIC overlap (484 of the 494
part-151 notice EPICs resolve into 2025 part 150).
Delhi's Okhla was +3. Do not copy a number between constituencies.

_note: All part numbers here are BASE-ROLL (old) numbers, because that is what
the register is keyed on. The UI shows both numberings side by side.
audit_min/max  — the parts in scope at all: searchable, with status tiles.
focus          — the parts the team is canvassing: the part picker and the
progress dashboard show only these. Widen when a new booth
draft_held     — base parts whose matching DRAFT roll we have actually
loaded. A part NOT listed here cannot be checked against
the draft, so its electors become CLEARED/assumed rather
than counted as removals. Add a part here only once its
parts._critical_manual: Parts pinned as critical regardless of the rule. Empty here; Delhi pinned one by hand.

_note: Paths are on the machine that runs the importers; they hold voter PII and
are never committed. Each SIR list names the BASE part it belongs to, and
the importer asserts that against the old part printed in the file.
missing_notice_parts records base parts we hold NO notice list for, so the
app can say so rather than silently reporting those electors as cleared.
import._excluded: notice_149.csv is 2026 part 149 = base part 148, which we have not OCR'd; 0 of its 699 EPICs appear in our roll.
